rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb keşt means removing a covering, like skinning an animal, peeling bark, or removing a veil from a face.
rows.anchor: “Keşt” kesilmiş bir hayvanın derisini yüzmek ve ağacın kabuğunu soymak ve yüzden nikābı sıyırmak gibi örtülü bir şeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stripping first evokes the total destruction of the upper cosmos, as in 21:104, but that is not his preferred contextual sense.
rows.anchor: يَوْمَ نَطْوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ [el-Enbiyâ 21/104] gibi âlem-i ulvînin tahrîbi ile fenâ-i küllî mânası tebâdür ederse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that the stripped heaven signify the unveiling of every reality in the newly established world after the heaven is folded.
rows.anchor: bundan murad semânın tayyından sonra كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍۢ نُّعِيدُهُۥ buyurduğu üzere yeni kurulacak olan o âlemde keşf-i gıtâ ve arz-ı küllî ile her hakikatin tecellîsi mânası olmak siyâk-ı beyâna daha muvâfıktır

rows.speaker: Tefsîr-i Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Nisaburi explains that the heaven is opened and removed, revealing Paradise and the Throne above it.
rows.anchor: semâ açılıp izâle olunarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the cover is removed, no worldly body or truth-obscuring thing remains; the Divine Throne appears and all reality is disclosed with certainty.
rows.anchor: Arş-ı Hak zâhir olup her hakikat hakka’l-yakīn münkeşif olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah's conclusion identifies this disclosure as the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: hâtimesiyle bunun din günü olduğu beyan olunarak bu mâna îzah edilecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human souls will stand between the manifestations of divine wrath and majesty and of divine mercy and beauty.
rows.anchor: nüfûs-ı insâniye Hakk’ın şu iki tecellîsi arasında bulunacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is intensely inflamed for the wicked through their bad deeds and God's anger.
rows.anchor: benî Âdem’in kötü amelleri ve Allah teâlâ’nın gazabı ile azgınlar için kızıştırılacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through divine grace and mercy, Paradise is brought near to the pious, adorned with the reward of their good deeds.
rows.anchor: fazl u rahmet-i ilâhiye ile güzel amellerin sevâbından donanmış olarak müttakīlere yaklaştırılacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These events occur at the final judgment immediately before the people of Hell and Paradise enter their respective destinations; the conditional wording assures their occurrence.
rows.anchor: son fasl-ı kazâ sırası olacak ve bunlar tahakkuka mevzû‘olan اِذَا ile ifade edildiği için muhakkak vukū‘bulacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding events, every soul will know what it prepared, whether good or evil, and what it did in the world.
rows.anchor: bir nefis ne hazırlamış olduğunu bilecektir. Hayır mı şer mi? İyi mi kötü mü? Dünyada ne yapmış, o gün için ne hazırlamış olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each deed, however small, is brought into its record, placed on its scale, and seen embodied before the soul.
rows.anchor: her amelin defterinde ihzar edilip mîzânına konduğu ve karşısında temessül ettiğini görecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is the answer to all the coordinated conditional clauses together, describing their combined extended period rather than each instant separately.
rows.anchor: Bu cümle اِذَا’ların atıf ile rabtından sonra hepsinin birden cevâbıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This awakening explains the saying that people sleep and wake when they die, and expresses the shock of resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: “İnsanlar uykudadırlar, öldükleri vakit uyanırlar”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the day when each soul finds its good and bad deeds present, as stated in 3:30.
rows.anchor: يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ مَّا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍۢ مُّحْضَرًۭا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِن سُوٓءٍۢ [Âl-i İmrân 3/30] buyurulan gün de bugündür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here nafs means each individual soul, and what is brought into presence is its good or bad deeds.
rows.anchor: burada da كُلّ نَفْس,نَفْسٌۭ meâlinde olarak “her bir nefis” demektir. İhzar edilen şey de iyi veya kötü amellerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds may be presented as written records or as distinct forms embodied in the afterlife according to their goodness or evil.
rows.anchor: dünyadaki amellerin iyilik ve kötülüklerine göre âhirette birer sûret-i mahsûsa ile temsil ve tecellî ederek huzurda bulundurulmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even in this world, a breath can take the form of fire, movement of light, or work of a building or garden; afterlife existence embodies the products of worldly deeds.
rows.anchor: Nitekim dünyada bile bir nefes bir ateş hâlinde, bir hareket bir ziyâ hâlinde veya bir binâ veya bahçe suretinde temessül eder.

rows.speaker: unnamed interpreters
rows.claim: Some interpreters held that wrongful consumption of an orphan's property literally means eating fire, without treating 4:10 as a simile.
rows.anchor: zulmen yetim malı yemenin hakikaten ateş yemek demek olduğuna kāil olanlar olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command brings deeds into presence, but because deeds are acquired by servants and presentation follows from them, presentation can figuratively be ascribed to the soul by causation.
rows.anchor: sebebiyet alâkasıyla nefs-i abde isnâdı da mecâzen sahih olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this clause, what a soul brought is, in reality, what it did; the wording assigns its worldly deeds and preparation for God's presence to the servant.
rows.anchor: nefs-i abde nazaran “mâ ahdarat” hakikatte “mâ amilet” mânasında olup her nefis dünyada iyi mi kötü mü ne yapmış olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing means finding every deed recorded in full detail without omission or seeing each deed's good or bad reality embodied, as 18:49 says.
rows.anchor: hayr u şer bütün amellerini defterinde hiçbir eksiksiz tafsîlâtıyla yazılı bulup hepsine muttali‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds enjoyed under worldly desire will appear ugly and painful, while difficult acts of obedience will appear beautiful and beloved.
rows.anchor: dünyada hevâ ve hevesine uygun gelerek hoş gördüğü birtakım amellerin o gün çirkin ve acı bir surette

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet likens disclosure to seeing, once dust clears, whether one's mount is a horse or a donkey.
rows.anchor: سَوْفَ تَرَى إِذَا انْجَ لَى الْغُبَارُ أَفَرَسٌ تَحْتَكَ أَمْ حِمَارُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the dust-clearing verse says, at the final unveiling a person will see whether worldly deeds lead to Hell or Paradise.
rows.anchor: o gün semâ sıyrılıp bütün hakikat münkeşif olduğu vakit insan da dünyada yaptığı amellerin kendisini cehenneme mi yoksa cennete mi götürdüğünü anlayacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This knowledge comes after the resurrection's opening of the records and stripping of heaven, not separately at each of the twelve events.
rows.anchor: bu biliş ve anlayış ise haber verilen on iki vaktin her birinde değil, neşr-i suhuf ve keşt-ı semâdan sonra olmak gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated conditional clauses each alert the reader to an independently awesome event; although a single opening conditional might suffice, the answer is attached to them collectively.
rows.anchor: her birinin müstakillen dehşet ve ehemmiyetine tenbih için اِذَا’lar tekrar edilmiş ve hüküm, mecmû‘una rabtolunmuştur.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a group's allegorical reading of the signs as metaphors for each human and the circumstances of death, including the sun as the self and stars as senses.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye tefsirinde demiştir ki: “Bir kavim bu zikrolunan şeylerin benî Âdem’den her biri ve ölüm sırasındaki ahvâl hakkında istiareler

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls this symbolic reading a doctrine of Batiniyya and extreme Sufis who attach themselves to Islam under cover while secretly rejecting it.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân da bunu naklettikten sonra şöyle demiştir: “Bu Bâtıniyye mezhebi ve gulât-ı sûfiyyeden İslâm’a müntesib olanların mezhebleridir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the Qur'an is clear Arabic and contains no symbols, riddles, inner meanings, or allusions to philosophical and naturalist teachings.
rows.anchor: Kitâbullah بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّۢ مُّبِينٍۢ [eş-Şu‘arâ 26/195] gelmiştir. Onda ne remiz ne lügaz ne bâtın yoktur.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan criticizes Fakhr al-Din al-Razi for inserting philosophers', astrologers', and astronomers' opinions into his commentary as far from Qur'anic exegesis.
rows.anchor: İbn Hatîb-i Rey nâmıyla mâruf Ebû Abdullâh Râzî

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan likewise objects to Sufi statements called 'truths' in Tahrir and Tahbir, some of which he says should not even be written.
rows.anchor: sâhibinin tefsir ettiği âyetlerin âhirinde sûfiyye müntesiblerinin kelâmlarından zikrettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Abu Hayyan's polemic is excessive and deficient in balance.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Ebû Hayyân’ın bu sözleri ifrat ve tefritten hâlî değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was revealed in clear Arabic, and its language is not itself an obscure symbolic code.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki Kelâmullah lisân-ı Arabî-i mübîn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A text should ordinarily be taken in its apparent sense unless a contextual indication prevents that reading.
rows.anchor: nusûsta aslolan bir karîne-i mâni‘a bulunmadıkça zâhiri üzere hamlolunmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alongside clear passages, the Qur'an has hidden, difficult, concise, and ambiguous passages and uses literal, figurative, explicit, implicit, allegorical, and rhetorical forms.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın ümmü’l-kitâb olan muhkemâtının yanında hafî, müşkil, mücmel ve müteşâbihâtı, hakikati, mecazı, sarîhi, kinâyesi, istiâresi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest sense remains intended, while further secondary implications may also be sought alongside it.
rows.anchor: Bütün bunlarda en vâzıh olan mâna maksud olmakla beraber “müstetbe‘ât-i terâkîb” denilen ve derece-i tâliyede matlub olan nice ifadeler de vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such secondary implications cannot contradict the clear explanation of decisive passages and are compatible with clear Arabic expression.
rows.anchor: zâhire münâfî ve münâkız olmayarak maiyyetinde bazı ihtimâlât ile derece-i tâliyede

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is wrong to claim the Qur'an contains no inner sense, symbol, or indication; the disconnected opening letters remain symbolic regardless of their interpretation.
rows.anchor: الٓمٓ، قٓ، نٓ gibi mukatta‘ât-ı süver ne suretle tefsir edilirse edilsin remzî olmaktan hâlî denemez.

rows.speaker: آثار
rows.claim: Some transmitted reports say the Qur'an has an outward and inward meaning, as well as a limit and a point of ascent.
rows.anchor: Doğrusu bazı âsârda dahi vârid olduğu üzere Kur’ân’ın hem zâhiri vardır hem bâtını, hem haddi vardır hem matla‘ı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outward and inward meanings cannot conflict, since the Qur'an is free of disagreement and contradiction, as 4:82 states.
rows.anchor: hakikatte ihtilâf ve tenakuzdan âzâde eblağ bir kitâb-ı mübîn olduğu için zâhiri ile bâtını arasında tehâlüf ve tebâyünden de münezzehtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting of outward and inward meanings resembles two seas meeting behind a boundary that prevents either from transgressing, as in 55:19–20.
rows.anchor: birbirine bağy u tecavüzüne mâni‘olan haddi aşılmamak şartıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritually inspired insights within those bounds have no end, just as the Lord's words exceed the sea's ink, as in 18:109.
rows.anchor: ondan zaman zaman vehbî ve zevkī olarak alınan tulû‘ât ve ilhâmâta bir nihâyet de tasavvur olunamaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is wrong to deny that the Qur'an has indications about human ideas and concerns, or to censure interpreters such as Razi for illuminating them.
rows.anchor: Râzî gibi o yolda tenvîr-i efkâra hizmet edenlere ta‘n etmek doğru olmadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufi commentaries that discuss spiritual insights without nullifying the text's clear sense and rulings should not all be classed with heretical esotericists.
rows.anchor: sûfiyye tefsirlerinin hepsini de Karâmita ve Hurûfiyye bâtıniyyesi gibi zenâdıkadan saymak da doğru değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashani and Ara'is should not be treated like Hasan Sabbah's and extreme Imamite books that nullify the Qur'an's outward meanings and rulings.
rows.anchor: mahza zâhirî olan me‘ânî ve ahkâmı ibtal vadisinde yazılmış Hasan Sabbah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abandoning decisive passages to pursue ambiguous ones for discord and distortive interpretation arises from a crooked heart, as 3:7 warns.
rows.anchor: kalb çarpıklığından, rûh bozukluğundan neş’et eden bir zeyğ u ilhaddır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignoring the insights of interpreters who first establish outward meanings and rulings, then offer compatible indications, would be a loss.
rows.anchor: sânihâtından istifade etmemek de mahrumiyet olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an addresses people according to their qualities and capacities, speaking to believers, thinkers, knowers, rememberers, the pious, and people of understanding at different levels.
rows.anchor: muhatabların evsâf ve kābiliyet-i mahsûsalarıyla derecelerine göre türlü mazmunlarla hitap edip dururken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentary's attention to intellectual and moral levels serves the Qur'an's aims of illumination and its levels of meaning.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın hadd ü matla‘ına ve umûmu tenvîre mâtuf olan makāsıdına uygun da olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excessive literalism is as harmful as excessive esotericism; the author invokes those learned in knowledge acting justly, as in 3:18.
rows.anchor: Her hâlde zâhirîlikte ifrat etmek de bâtınîlikte ifrat etmek kadar muzırdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an includes both tafsir and ta'wil.
rows.anchor: Ve Kur’an’da tefsir de vardır, tevil de vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People ruled by whim can deny everything, even the sun.
rows.anchor: kendi fikr ü hevâsına saplanıp da Güneş’i inkâra kadar gidenler her şeyi inkâr edebilirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and stars should first be believed in according to their real, apparent meanings because no rational or transmitted evidence bars that reading.
rows.anchor: Şems ve nücûmu evvelemirde kendi hakīkī mânalarıyla anlamaya mâni‘olacak aklî ve naklî hiçbir karîne olmadığı için bunlara zâhir ve hakikati vechile inanmak lâzımdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering literal and figurative possibilities for the sun's folding and stars' dimming, including broader indications, does not conflict with belief in their real events.
rows.anchor: tekvir ve inkidârın sûret-i vukū‘una nazaran mânalarındaki hakīkī ve mecâzî ihtimalleri mülâhaza etmek bu imana münâfî olmayacağı gibi

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Qurtubi reads the mention of abandoned pregnant camels as metaphor and representation, not as an obscure symbol contrary to clear expression.
rows.anchor: Kurtubî kelâmın istiare ve temsil üzerine olduğunu söylemekle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering possible metaphors in events whose details remain unknown is neither illegitimate symbolism nor esoteric deviation; it helps make the great resurrection imaginable through the lesser events and strengthen faith.
rows.anchor: Bilakis kıyâmet-i kübrâ vukū‘âtını kıyâmet-i suğrâ vukū‘âtıyla ezhâna takrib ederek imanı takviyeye çalışmaktır.

rows.speaker: Nizâmüddîn Nîsâbûrî
rows.claim: Nisaburi first interprets these verses according to their apparent sense, then records the interpreters' reflections on the lesser resurrection.
rows.anchor: Nizâmüddîn Nîsâbûrî Garâibu’l-Kur’ân ve Regāibu’l-Furkān nâm tefsirinde bu âyetleri zâhiri vechile usul dairesinde tefsir ettikten sonra ehl-i tevilin zikri geçen kavillerini de şöyle kaydetmiştir:

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The interpreters apply these events to the lesser resurrection, the state of death.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i tevil dediler ki bu ahvâli kıyâmet-i suğrâ hakkında da itibar etmek mümkindir. Kıyâmet-i suğrâ ise mevt hâlidir.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The sun represents the rational soul, and its folding is the severing of the soul's attachment.
rows.anchor: Şems nefs-i nâtıkadır. Tekvîri, onun ta‘allukunun kesilmesidir.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The dimming of the stars represents the collapse of the soul's faculties.
rows.anchor: İnkidâr-ı nücûm kuvvelerin tesâkutudur.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The moving mountains represent the separation of the chief bodily organs from their functions.
rows.anchor: Tesyîr-i cibâl a‘zâ-yı reîsenin

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The pregnant camels represent the body, whose order is neglected at death.
rows.anchor: Işâr, bedendir. O vakit emri ihmal olunur.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The gathering of wild beasts represents the emergence in a person of the results of beastly and predatory acts.
rows.anchor: Haşr-ı vuhûş şahıs üzerinde behîmî ve sebü‘î

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The kindling of the seas represents the end of false imaginings and empty hopes, which have no shore except voluntary or involuntary death.
rows.anchor: Tescîr-i bihâr, evhâm-ı bâtılenin ve boş emellerin tükenmesidir.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The pairing of souls represents each disposition joining its own kind, darkness with darkness and light with light.
rows.anchor: Tezvîc-i nüfûs her melekenin kendi cinsine; zulmetin zulmete, nûrun nûra inzımâmıdır.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The buried girl represents a capacity that an accountable person wastes on something other than its created purpose.
rows.anchor: Mev’ûde, mükellefin mâ-hulika-lehinin gayride zâyi‘ettiği kuvvedir.

rows.speaker: some of the author's verifying teachers
rows.claim: Some of the author's teachers also said the buried girl represents any issue that occurs to the mind but disappears without being written down.
rows.anchor: Üstazlarımdan olan bazı muhakkikīnden o, hatıra sünuh edip de kitabet ile kaydedilmeyerek gāib olmuş olan her meseledir diye de işittim.

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The heaven represents the world of spirits; the other signs retain their apparent senses.
rows.anchor: Semâ da semâ-yı ervâhtır, bâkīsi zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpreters' readings do not deny the great resurrection; they also draw lessons about the certain lesser resurrection of death, which benefits faith and creed.
rows.anchor: muradları bu âyetlerin esas itibariyle kıyâmet-i kübrâ hakkında olduğunu nefy ü inkâr değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on the death of an individual and the death of a community, the lesser and middle resurrections, is instructive; each shares in the awakening announced here and previews the greater resurrection.
rows.anchor: bunların hepsinde عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌۭ مَّآ أَحْضَرَتْ’dan bir intibah hissesi vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these reflections culminate in the great resurrection, the verses' true subject, when reality is fully unveiled and every soul knows its deeds at final judgment.
rows.anchor: hepsinin tamamı kıyâmet-i kübrâdadır. Ve bu âyetler, asıl onun hakkındadır. Bütün hakk u hakikatin inkişâfı
